newsitem.title: USA: "All of Me" Composer Gerald Marks dies at age 96.
newsitem.headline: "All of Me" Composer Gerald Marks dies at age 96.

text.p: Composer Gerald Marks, whose songs included "All of Me" and "Is It True What They Say About Dixie," died at his home here at age 96 on Monday, friends said.
Marks, who was born in Saginaw, Michigan, started writing songs at age 10 and kept on writing until just before he died.
The biggest hit he had in his 86-year-long career was "All of Me," which he cowrote with bandleader and frequent collaborator Seymour Simons.

Simons' son Rody said "All of Me," written in 1931, was recorded in 2,000 different versions, including four by Frank Sinatra. A version by Willie Nelson lasted 10 years on the charts. Also recording it were Mae West, Duke Ellington and Ella Fitzgerald.
Marks wrote "Is it True What They Say About Dixie" for Al Jolson and it became a number one song.
Marks also wrote music for poet Carl Sandburg and collaborated with Gen. Omar Bradley on a series of patriotic songs.
